chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Cod liver oil in Scandinavia
summary: A Norwegian man gave him cod liver oil that cured his coughs for ten years; he takes it still and his 14-year-old son loves it.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And we weren't used to it. So one

Norwegian guy told me when we were in Oslo, and I said, "Oh, that cough again." He said, "Listen, I'm going to tell you something." So he took me to the apothek they call it, the drug store, and bought me a great bottle of cod liver oil, pure cod liver oil. He said, "Now, you take this three times a day, when you get up, when you have lunch, and before you go to bed. Just take the bottle up and take three big gulps." Boy, that thing -- I didn't have a cold for about 10 years after that.
I didn't even have a sniffle.
Fancy that. I know that -- you know, that's a remedy in England, too, you know.
So I tried to -- but William said, "I can't stand the taste of that." And I said, "But you should." And I know that I should take it, so I'm going to adapt myself to this taste, you know.
I made up my mind and I'm going to like it.
And in fact my son, he loves it.
Oh, he loves it. When he gets up in the morning, before he goes to school, he says, 'Oh, I have to take my oil.'
And I tell him stories about, you know, about being up north in Scandinavia and how it saved my life.
And how it's good for you, it makes your bones strong and so forth. He loves it.
So we have to have it for him all the time.
But I continued to take it until -- oh, I still take a little sip now and then.
Uh-huh. I used to start taking it around the first of October until the last part of February, then I'd stop.
But it would carry me through and I'd never have a cold, never, never never.
No. Fancy that. Well, listen Kenny, well that's more or less what I wanted to ask you about. I wanted to know what kind of effect it had on you, you know, what kind of reaction you had to it.
